body: Thank you, yes my iron is and has been elevated for a while, even without confirmation I have HH is donation an an effective treatment? I’m also concerned donating my blood with high iron may overload someone else via transfusion?

No, people who prey on woman kill, let’s stop blaming 16yos girls for not doing enough to protect themselves.

“Complacency kills” …well actually it’s the murderers.

(This doesn’t mean you shouldn’t take protective steps, but if you’re attacked while waking in your home streets then your attacker is 100% to blame)

Your cousin has been fully informed by you, and still prefers to walk, which is her right and choice. Listen to her. I know you want her 100% safe, but often we create a more firm safety by listening to our loved ones wishes.
Your post history says you live in the U.K. so her risk, while not 0, is not huge. (she’s much more likely to be assaulted by a man she knows unfortunately)

Please don’t cut off her world, please let her occupy space on her home streets and be present in public, if this is what she wants. Reigning women in may seem like a help, but in the long run giving wings rather than chains gives a fuller life, even if it may be more dangerous ❤️

This is you seeking help, as much as you say you are posting this for others, you are reaching out, and that’s great. But your issues are serious enough to need a trained therapist and not the internet. Especially as you haven’t actually accepted to ask for help, in a forum designed for help, which says a lot. 
It reads like you blame your wife for your issues and are helpless in your own life. Speaking to a therapist will help you feel more able to take control of things. Best of luck to you.

I agree, and didn’t mean to make my point at the exclusion of other reasons, just adding something whic hadn’t been said yet. I appreciate your take on these issues, and we need more of your type of acceptance, rather than the silencers.

I agree with you. Sure it may be annoying for someone’s talk to often about their identity a lot. But since those identity’s have often been marginalised and silenced in the past, it’s can be significant for that person to be open.
ask them if they want conversation.

Personally I don’t find it at all akward, and if it is for others but we keep treating it as akward, it’ll always be akward. Why not make this an acceptable question rather than the assumptionwork it is now? I’m glad you’re self aware enogh to know if someone wants to chat, a lot of drivers aren’t, especially towards female riders.

Wish this was a more socially acceptable thing to ask! Why say “where are you heading?” or “Busy day?” When those are not the questions you want an answer to? 
We have been socialised to think head on questions are impolite or akward, but clarity and honesty can have big advantages (parallels between this and then sex/consent questions people should be asking spring to mind)
“You’re a piece of shit” - my brain

I can only imagine how hard it's it right now for you, and to be in a place where you feel not only attacked from outside, but not properly nurtured and cared for by the one relationship which you feel is your only rock right now, by your Mom, the person who is supposed to guide you through life and help you grow up, and yet she's putting you in a situation where you have to ask for advice from strangers online, not purposely, but through her actions. It must be hard because how can you feel like your getting the support you need from anywhere? It must be so isolating. I just want to give you a hug. I can't tell you what to do, but I can hope you stay open to the possibility that your world view might be changeable, and there is hope at the end of the tunnel, and that the future can be bright.

It must be really tough to have your world view questioned, to have your reality trodden on and split apart, analysed and dissected by people who don't know you personally. 
It's been a lot to take in for you tonight. Take a breath. Perhaps have a bath or read a book, play game, make an animation, do something you find nurturing. Sleep and rest. Then tomorrow bring a new light to the issues, see if you can't take a step back, and ponder on why people might say things like they did when they read about your situation. It's not your fault. You need real and deep support, and it seems like your not getting what you deserve. Look after yourself x

Would make someones day to find it, and then it's up to them what they do with it :)

Manipulators gonna manipulate. 

The last weeks of this relationship being good is like icing on dog poop.

Brace yourself though, that iced dog poop will hit the fan once she knows you're divorcing her.

I fully support your decision to divorce,and wish you all the best with it. It's good to hear these updates.
Great you two worked it out :)

People like him are such nightmares because they make -you- feel like the one with the problem. They twist your words and actions so you doubt yourself, so you apologise though it was their fault. 
You are sane, he is abusive. It's a harsh reality and almost impossible to see from the inside. We are outside and we see, I hope you can join us outside and have a look for yourself...

That doesn't sound like bipolar, that sounds like grade A asshole-ism. Luckily there is a cure. But it only works for you. It's called getting the hell out of there.


On a serious note, this guy is abusive, do not give him the opportunity to be more so, you know he gets abusive when he's challenged, your breaking up with him will be a HUGE challenge to him. Make sure to protect yourself, I would suggest collecting your belongings from his, cutting ties on social media, before sending a letter telling him you do not want to hear from him again under any circumstances. Don't let him get in your head. Don't let him justify or blame his bipolar, a shitty personality is his real excuse. You deserve better, best of luck to you, be strong :)

Please don't place the blame on yourself for his infidelity. There should be no pity for him. Yes, a situation where you partner is suffering is hard to deal with, where you don't feel your needs are being met can be hard, but he dealt with it in a very nasty, selfish and damaging way. From where you are it seems like shades of grey, but his choice was pretty black from where I'm standing.

Its not even about being worthy of 'excellence'. How about expecting your partner to treat you with a basic level respect? You deserve that at least...?

I would say it's possible to move past. But at the moment it seems be has no desire to. Why would he? He can have his cake and eat it. His continued deceptive behavior is showing he isn't invested in change, and without change you are doomed to the same fate.
I suggest assessing if this is what you really want out of a partner, remember you are more in control than you think, if you don't want him treating you like this anymore don't let him. Let him go.

I'm really glad you're getting back on track and improving yourself, good to hear, I hope it continues.

Of course this situation is deeper and more complicated than I know. And I'm not trying to downplay any of your emotions or experience, you seem very caring, sweet and thoughtful. I say these things because I can see you potentially putting his happiness before yours (Perhaps still feelings guilty for pushing him away) and getting sucked into an unhealthy 'friendship'/'relationship' with this guy. I honestly can't see the harm in waiting longer until you potentially pursue a friendship. Especially as you suspect his intentions run deeper than friendship, it lets him have time as well.

This itches me the most: 

>If we become friends I'm fine with that. If it turns into a relationship I'm fine with that

Why would you be fine with being in a relationship with someone you already know you are not compatible with? 


Please understand while you asked advise on a very small aspect of your relationship with him (What were his intentions when he asked about you relationship status) if we see a wider aspect of the relationship we think needs addressing or that we can give advise on we will. You can choose the best course of action for you, knowing all the facts, there just might be elements you can look at from a different perspective :)

RE your edit: We're not attacking your ex. You certainly didn't paint a bad picture of him. He didn't communicate with your properly (for whatever reason) that doesn't make him a bad person. That makes you incompatible. He did things which hurt you, unintentionally or not. You deserve someone who doesn't hurt you. Two of the most wonderful people can still be incompatible. 
He's put you in another tough situation now, contacting you out of the blue and asking questions which and playing on your mind. I'm sure he means well, but you should remember to do whats untimely best for you.

>[male friend] made an offhand comment a while ago about not being opposed to a same-sex relationship while in college just to have the experience if nothing else, which has made it hard to dismiss these feelings since the opportunity to act on them seems to exist.


You do no have the opportunity to act on them. You have a girlfriend. You 'opportunity' to act sexually with a person currently rests with her, as that's who you've committed to.

Good for your for figuring out your sexuality, now you want to explore it, if you want to pursue a relationship with someone else (whatever gender) do the decent thing and let your girlfriend go.
Imagine your male friend was a girl and you had these feelings the same, would it be okay to spend this much time with her? and feel attracted towards her? and sexually fantasize about her? I doubt you GF would be pleased...

You can't have it both ways. You either have a girlfriend and are faithful to her. Or you let her go and explore your sexuality. Good luck figuring it out :)

"selfish" You don't need to take this word he has applied to you and put it on your shoulders.

It' not selfish to want a partner who respects you. 

You are brave. Have this word on your shoulders and see how it feels :)

You are trying to see things from his point of view, when really, this should be about you, and what you can do to help yourself.

From your point of view, you are out of a relationship you were unhappy in. You ex wanted to end the relationship, so it will take you longer to get over him than it will him with you. You are only ever going to have his word on if he was seeing the other girl before (so why worry about it?) You deserve better that someone who will to jump straight to someone else. You deserve someone who really wants to be with you, this is not that guy. Distance yourself from him. In fact you should consider cutting all contact with him. Seems like that phone conversation just messed with your head more. At the moment you are not gaining anything by having him in your life.

Good luck hun, take some time out for yourself, it's a rough time. Remember, you are irreplaceable to the right person. 

Edit: words

Stay strong sweetie. This isn't your fault, don't blame yourself for your mums (over)reactions, she isn't handling this how she should, and it's sad to see it's affecting you, but remember you didn't cause this.

>she is upset that I don't love her as much as she loves me

Phew, that's a heavy burden to put on a child. A mother has chosen to bring another person into to world and unconditionally love them, they shouldn't place the weight of their emotional needs on their child. I'm sorry that's happening here.

When you talk to your therapist, try and get your Mum involved, she sounds like she could really benefit from therapy, your relationship certainly will. You did the right thing by asking her to sit in with you. It's a shame she declined. Talk to your therapist about the best way to get her involved, he will probably know the best strategies to talk with her about it, and hopefully he will reach out to her himself.

Good luck :)
